key_insight: A lifting-based kinematic decomposition lets Dirichlet boundary velocities be enforced strongly in structure-preserving elastodynamics, avoiding DAE constraints while retaining an ODE form.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical FEM pathway for accurate boundary-actuated solid dynamics models with better boundary fidelity and cleaner time integration.
method: Split displacement/velocity into a boundary-vanishing dynamic part plus a prescribed lifting field.
Embed the lifting map into virtual power to derive lifted port-Hamiltonian models.
Discretize into 2-field and 4-field FEM formulations that recover standard matrix partitioning under specific shape functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations validating energy balance properties and computational performance, and shows equivalence to classic FEM algebraic partitioning in suitable cases.
watch_item: The approach depends on choosing an appropriate lifting function/shape-function structure, so implementation quality at the boundary may be sensitive to discretization design.
paper_title: Strong imposition of Dirichlet boundary velocities in structure-preserving discretizations of elastodynamics
